newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Senate approves post-WW2 pact with Germany.
newsitem.headline: Czech Senate approves post-WW2 pact with Germany.

text.p: The Czech upper house of parliament, the Senate, gave final approval on Wednesday to a post-World War Two reconciliation pact with Germany, the CTK news agency said.
The measure, already signed by both governments and approved by Germany's parliament and the Czech lower house, was approved in the Senate by a vote of 54 to 25 after only a few hours of debate.
The Senate approval did not include a preamble, which was attached to the resolution accompanying the declaration in the lower house.
In the declaration, Bonn expresses its regret for the 1938-45 occupation of Czech lands and Prague its sorrow for excessive brutality in the expulsion of ethnic Germans after the war.

It was quickly approved by a large majority in the German parliament but faced virulent attacks by Czech Communist and Republican deputies in the lower house who said the measure was a sellout to Bonn. Debate dragged on for four days before the lower house approved the measure by a large majority.
The Czech government, which has only a minority in the lower house, has a strong majority in the Senate.
